sentences.zh: 几乎就像护身符一样，劳作了一整天后，晚上在烛光下阅读，或者在

sentences.en: But the reason we wanted to focus on the Speller was because of the profound impact this book would
sentences.zh: 但我们之所以想把目光聚焦在这本拼字书上，是因为这本书对

sentences.zh: 美国历史上两位最具影响力的黑人男性产生了深远的影响。

sentences.zh: 他们的分歧实质上将美国黑人知识界一分为二。

sentences.zh: 与W·E·B·

sentences.zh: 他们的竞争并非出于私怨。

sentences.zh: 这是围绕美国最迫切问题展开的一场

sentences.en: America.

sentences.zh: 自由究竟意味着什么？

sentences.zh: 又该如何为之奋斗？

sentences.en: Do you demand everything right
sentences.zh: 你是要立刻

sentences.en: now?

sentences.zh: 还是在体制内一步一个脚印地努力，等待时机？

sentences.zh: 通过他们

sentences.zh: 这场至今依然激烈的争论的分歧所在。

sentences.en: Let's start with Booker T.
sentences.zh: 让我们从布克·T·

sentences.en: Washington.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿开始说起。

sentences.en: He was born into slavery and later freed when news of emancipation reached the plantation
sentences.zh: 他出生于奴隶制家庭，后来当解放的消息传到他和他家人

sentences.en: where he and his family were held.
sentences.zh: 被囚禁的种植园时，他重获自由。

sentences.zh: 布克唯一的愿望就是识字，但现实中他却不得不

sentences.en: work in a salt mine to help support his family.
sentences.zh: 在盐矿工作以补贴家用。

sentences.en: To make matters worse, he could see and hear happy
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，从他在矿上的工作地点望出去，

sentences.en: children passing to and from school mornings and afternoons from where he was working in the mines.
sentences.zh: 他每天早晚都能看到欢快的孩子们上学放学，从路边走过。

sentences.en: So he asks his mother for help.
sentences.zh: 于是他向母亲寻求帮助。

sentences.en: His mother got her hands on a Blueback Speller for him
sentences.zh: 他的母亲设法为他弄来了一本《蓝皮拼字书》，

sentences.en: and he treated it as, you know, as a kind of magical document.
sentences.zh: 而他把它当成了一种，你知道的，某种神奇的宝典。

sentences.en: He taught himself to read with it
sentences.zh: 他靠这本书自学了阅读，

sentences.en: and it really shaped his life.
sentences.zh: 这确实重塑了他的一生。

sentences.en: This is the very first book that Booker holds in his hand
sentences.zh: 这是布克手中拿过的第一本书，

sentences.en: and it changes the course of his life.
sentences.zh: 它改变了他的人生轨迹。

sentences.en: There's this trajectory from his mother finding this book
sentences.zh: 从他的母亲为他找到这本书，

sentences.en: for him and he thinking that this is sort of the greatest possible, you know, object that he could
sentences.zh: 到他认为这是他所能拥有的，你知道的，最伟大的物品，再到最终成为

sentences.en: have and then becoming ultimately the most powerful Black man in the United States.
sentences.zh: 全美最有权势的黑人，这是一条清晰的发展轨迹。

sentences.en: After teaching himself to read using the Blueback Speller, he attends night school after working in the
sentences.zh: 通过《蓝皮拼字书》自学阅读后，他在盐矿工作了一整天，

sentences.en: salt mines all day.
sentences.zh: 接着还要去上夜校。

sentences.en: Then in 1872, at age 16, he makes his way to Hampton Institute, which is one of
sentences.zh: 然后，在1872年，16岁的他前往汉普顿学院，

sentences.en: the first schools established for African Americans in Virginia.
sentences.zh: 这是弗吉尼亚州最早为非裔美国人建立的学校之一。

sentences.en: He has to walk, I think it's something
sentences.zh: 我想他不得不步行

sentences.en: like 500 miles to get to Hampton Institute, you know, so this passion, this drive for education is
sentences.zh: 大约500英里才到达汉普顿学院，你看，这种对教育的热情和驱动力

sentences.en: extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 是非同寻常的。

sentences.en: And then he becomes the first principal and then later on what would be president
sentences.zh: 随后他成为了塔斯基吉学院的首任校长，也就是后来的

sentences.en: of Tuskegee Institute, now Tuskegee University.
sentences.zh: 塔斯基吉大学（现为塔斯基吉大学）。

sentences.en: On the 4th of July of 1881, Washington arrived at
sentences.zh: 在1881年的7月4日，华盛顿抵达

sentences.en: Tuskegee as its first principal.
sentences.zh: 塔斯基吉，担任首任校长。

sentences.en: But the school existed in name only.
sentences.zh: 但当时的学校仅存於名义之上。

sentences.en: The state of Alabama had
sentences.zh: 亚拉巴马州

sentences.en: allocated just $2,000 a year to pay the teachers.
sentences.zh: 每年仅拨款2000美元用于支付教师薪水。

sentences.en: There was no land, no buildings, no equipment,
sentences.zh: 这里没有土地，没有建筑物，没有设备，

sentences.en: just some cash and an idea on paper.
sentences.zh: 只有一些现金和纸上谈兵的一个构想。

sentences.en: So Washington shows up and just starts teaching,
sentences.zh: 于是华盛顿一到这就开始上课，

sentences.en: at first out of a one-room shanty.
sentences.zh: 起初是在一间单房的小木屋里授课。

sentences.en: It was in such disrepair that whenever it rained,
sentences.zh: 那间木屋破烂不堪，每逢下雨，

sentences.en: one of the students would have to hold an umbrella over Washington's head for the rest of the lesson.
sentences.zh: 就会有一名学生不得不举着伞站在华盛顿头顶，好让他上完剩下的课。

sentences.en: Shortly after that, Washington borrows some money to buy an abandoned 100-acre former plantation,
sentences.zh: 在那之后不久，华盛顿借钱买下了一处废弃的、占地100英亩的前种植园，

sentences.en: and he and the students build Tuskegee with their own hands, brick by brick.
sentences.zh: 他和学生们亲手一砖一瓦地建造了塔斯基吉。

sentences.en: As in,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，

sentences.en: they literally make the bricks themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们真的是自己烧砖。

sentences.en: But it isn't easy.
sentences.zh: 但这并不容易。

sentences.en: The first brick kiln fails,
sentences.zh: 第一座砖窑失败了，

sentences.en: then the second, then the third.
sentences.zh: 接着是第二座，然后是第三座。

sentences.en: At one point, he pawns his watch for $15 just to keep the experiment
sentences.zh: 有一次，为了维持实验继续下去，

sentences.en: going.
sentences.zh: 他甚至把自己的手表当了15美元。

sentences.en: For Washington, it's a lesson in the dignity of labor.
sentences.zh: 对华盛顿而言，这是一场关于劳动的尊严的深刻一课。

sentences.en: And it gets to his core idea
sentences.zh: 这也切中了他在教育方面的

sentences.en: about education.
sentences.zh: 核心理念。

sentences.en: Instead of teaching the humanities, he thought education should be focused on giving
sentences.zh: 他认为教育不应教授人文学科，而应专注于赋予

sentences.en: Black people practical skills, a philosophy known as industrial education.
sentences.zh: 黑人实用技能，这种哲学被称为实业教育。

sentences.en: So Tuskegee becomes this institution through the leadership of Booker T.
sentences.zh: 因此，在布克·T·华盛顿的领导下，塔斯基吉成为了

sentences.en: Washington that is a model
sentences.zh: 实业教育的

sentences.en: of industrial education.
sentences.zh: 典范机构。

sentences.en: So engineering, animal husbandry, agricultural work and the like.
sentences.zh: 教授诸如工程学、畜牧业、农业等内容。

sentences.en: Things
sentences.zh: 比如

sentences.en: like learning how to build porches, appropriate ventilation for housing.
sentences.zh: 学习如何建造门廊、如何为房屋设计合适的通风系统。

sentences.en: How do you grow crops to
sentences.zh: 如何种植农作物

sentences.en: appropriately feed the community?
sentences.zh: 来为社区提供充足的食物？

sentences.en: How do you take care of the land?
sentences.zh: 如何爱护土地？

sentences.en: Not everyone agreed that these were the most important things to be learning.
sentences.zh: 并非所有人都赞同这些是最重要的学习内容。

sentences.en: For many Black
sentences.zh: 对许多黑人

sentences.en: families, it felt like settling.
sentences.zh: 家庭来说，这感觉像是妥协。

sentences.en: After generations of being denied literacy, why not go all in on
sentences.zh: 在历经几代人被剥夺识字权之后，为什么不全力投入

sentences.en: classical education?
sentences.zh: 古典教育呢？

sentences.en: Why not Latin, philosophy, literature, everything that had been kept out of
sentences.zh: 为什么不去学习拉丁语、哲学、文学，以及所有那些长期以来

sentences.en: reach for so long?
sentences.zh: 遥不可及的东西？

sentences.en: But Washington was also thinking strategically.
sentences.zh: 但华盛顿同时也在进行战略层面的思考。

sentences.en: In a country still shaped by Jim Crow,
sentences.zh: 在一个依然深受吉姆·克劳法影响的国家里，

sentences.en: where reconstruction efforts had failed and been abandoned.
sentences.zh: 那里的重建努力已经失败并被放弃。

sentences.en: He believed pushing for industrial
sentences.zh: 他坚信，推动实业教育

sentences.en: education was more likely to be tolerated, less likely to provoke backlash.
sentences.zh: 更有可能被社会容忍，也更不容易激起反弹。

sentences.en: Industrial education was
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，实业教育

sentences.en: conceived of as less threatening in many ways than classical education for Black Americans, because classical
sentences.zh: 被认为比古典教育对美国黑人构成的威胁更小，因为古典教育

sentences.en: education was what the most elite white Americans, that kind of education they received.
sentences.zh: 正是那些精英白人美国人所接受的教育。

sentences.en: Booker T.
sentences.zh: 布克·T·

sentences.en: Washington was advocating for this education that keeps people working in relationship to the land,
sentences.zh: 华盛顿所倡导的是这种让人们继续与土地打交道的教育，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: That's part of why it's seen as less threatening.
sentences.zh: 这也是它被认为威胁较小的原因之一。

sentences.en: Underneath that educational philosophy,
sentences.zh: 在这种教育哲学背后，

sentences.en: there was a more controversial political idea.
sentences.zh: 隐藏着一个更具争议的政治观点。

sentences.en: Washington believed that economic self-sufficiency
sentences.zh: 华盛顿认为，经济上的自给自足

sentences.en: had to come before the push for full civil rights.
sentences.zh: 必须先于争取完全的公民权利。

sentences.en: He did not believe in immediately pressing
sentences.zh: 他不主张立即为非裔美国人争取

sentences.en: for access to suffrage and other kinds of civil rights for African Americans and instead focused on economic
sentences.zh: 选举权和其他种类的公民权利，而是将重点放在经济

sentences.en: development, land acquisition and the like.
sentences.zh: 发展、土地购置等方面。

sentences.en: And this philosophy?
sentences.zh: 而这种哲学？

sentences.en: This philosophy was about to make him
sentences.zh: 这种哲学即将使他成为

sentences.en: one of the most famous men in America.
sentences.zh: 美国最著名的人物之一。

sentences.en: And the thing that would do it was a single speech delivered on a single
sentences.zh: 而成就这一切的，是1895年在亚特兰大

sentences.en: afternoon in Atlanta in 1895.
sentences.zh: 一个下午发表的一场演讲。

sentences.en: The city was hosting a World's Fair and had invited Booker T.
sentences.zh: 当时该市正在举办世界博览会，并邀请了布克·T·

sentences.en: Washington
sentences.zh: 华盛顿

sentences.en: to speak.
sentences.zh: 前去演讲。

sentences.en: By then, Washington had become a rare figure, a Black leader that Southerners felt comfortable
sentences.zh: 到那时，华盛顿已成为一个罕见的人物——一个让南方人感到安心的黑人领袖，

sentences.en: with, comfortable enough to put him on stage.
sentences.zh: 安心到足以让他登上演讲台。

sentences.en: Picture it.
sentences.zh: 想象一下这个场景。

sentences.en: The late afternoon sun is pouring into his eyes
sentences.zh: 午后斜阳刺痛着他的双眼，

sentences.en: as he steps to the podium.
sentences.zh: 而他正走向讲台。

sentences.en: Gilmore's band plays the Star-Spangled Banner.
sentences.zh: 吉尔摩乐队演奏了《星条旗》。

sentences.en: And then, Dixie.
sentences.zh: 然后是《迪克西》。

sentences.en: Thousands are staring at this Black man about to address a white Southern audience on a national stage,
sentences.zh: 成千上万的人盯着这位即将向全国舞台上的白人南方观众发表演讲的黑人男子，

sentences.en: something that had likely never happened before in that part of the country.
sentences.zh: 这在该地区的那个地方很可能以前从未发生过。

sentences.en: This famous or infamous speech that he delivers in 1895, in which he says that Black and white Americans
sentences.zh: 他在1895年发表了这篇著名或声名狼藉的演讲，其中他提到黑人和白人美国人

sentences.en: can be as separate as fingers on a hand and implicitly foregoes advocacy for civil and political rights
sentences.zh: 可以像手掌上的手指一样分立，并含蓄地放弃了对公民权利和政治权利的主张

sentences.en: and instead, you know, encourages Black Americans to cast down their buckets where they were
sentences.zh: 取而代之的是，你知道的，鼓励黑人美国人在他们所在的地方扎根

sentences.en: and don't worry about how their rights are being systematically denied them in the South.
sentences.zh: 而不要去担心他们在南方是如何被系统性地剥夺权利的。

sentences.en: A reporter who was there wrote it up for the New York World, and he replays this moment.
sentences.zh: 当时在场的一位记者为《纽约世界报》撰文，重现了这一时刻。

sentences.en: Where Washington lifts up his hand, his hand representing society.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿举起他的手，这只手代表着社会。

sentences.en: He spreads his fingers apart and says
sentences.zh: 他张开手指说道

sentences.en: to the audience, in all things purely social, we can be as separate as fingers on a hand.
sentences.zh: 对观众说，在所有纯粹的社交事务上，我们可以像手掌上的手指一样分立。

sentences.en: As in, white people and Black people don't need to mix.
sentences.zh: 意思是，白人和黑人不需要融合。

sentences.en: We can stay segregated and still work towards the same goal.
sentences.zh: 我们可以保持隔离，却依然能朝着同一个目标努力。

sentences.en: It was a simple and effective metaphor for the fiction of separate but equal.
sentences.zh: 对于“别具一格却又平等”的虚妄幻想，这是一个简单而有效的隐喻。

sentences.en: And white America loved it.
sentences.zh: 而白人美国人对此喜爱有加。

sentences.en: It gave them exactly what they wanted.
sentences.zh: 这正好给了他们想要的东西。

sentences.en: The comfort of segregation without the guilt.
sentences.zh: 享受隔离的舒适感，而没有内疚感。

sentences.en: Social separation without moral responsibility.
sentences.zh: 没有道德责任的社交隔离。

sentences.en: And the crowd goes into what the reporter calls a delirium of applause.
sentences.zh: 人群陷入了记者所称的狂热掌声中。

sentences.en: Hats in the air.
sentences.zh: 帽子飞向空中。

sentences.en: Handkerchiefs waving.
sentences.zh: 手帕在挥舞。

sentences.en: Everyone on their feet.
sentences.zh: 所有人都站了起来。

sentences.en: The speech is a rousing success in mainstream America because, in many ways, you know, it's 1895,
sentences.zh: 这场演讲在主流美国社会大获成功，因为在很多方面，你知道的，那是1895年，

sentences.en: so it's some years past the end of Reconstruction, which completely ended by 1877.
sentences.zh: 所以距离重建期结束已经过了好几年，重建期在1877年就彻底结束了。

sentences.en: But in the intervening years, Jim Crow is becoming more deeply entrenched in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但在随后的几年里，吉姆·克劳法在美利坚

sentences.en: South and really in many ways across the country.
sentences.zh: 南方变得根深蒂固，在很多方面实际上也遍及全国。

sentences.en: And by that I mean not just segregated facilities, but also segregated forms of employment, really control of the labor of African Americans.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不仅是隔离的设施，还有隔离的就业形式，以及对非裔美国人劳动力真正的控制。

sentences.en: The beginning of, we see, sort of fundamentally unequals experiences with relationship to law enforcement and the like.
sentences.zh: 我们开始看到，在执法等方面，出现了一种根本上不平等的经历。

sentences.en: And so it is a speech that has this sort of mythology to it that if Black Americans just work really hard and put their heads down
sentences.zh: 因此，这篇演讲带有这样一种神话色彩：如果黑人美国人只是非常努力地工作，埋头苦干，

sentences.en: and stop pushing against the way that society is becoming increasingly more oppressive and restrictive, then things will get better.
sentences.zh: 不再去抗争那日益压抑和限制重重的社会现状，事情就会好转。

sentences.en: And it not only lets the South off the hook, but it lets the federal government off the hook, which is in some ways has already abandoned African Americans
sentences.zh: 这不仅让南方卸下了包袱，也让联邦政府卸下了包袱，联邦政府在某些方面已经放弃了非裔美国人

sentences.en: in the advocacy for the rights that they were granted after the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 不再为他们在内战后被赋予的权利进行辩护。

sentences.en: You might have learned about this speech in school.
sentences.zh: 你可能在学校里学过这篇演讲。

sentences.en: It becomes known as the Atlanta Compromise, because compromise is what many people hear in it, whether or not that's all Washington intended.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“亚特兰大妥协”，因为无论华盛顿的本意是否完全如此，很多人在这篇演讲中听到的都是妥协。

sentences.en: I mean, it absolutely didn't represent the totality of Washington's thought.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这绝对不能代表华盛顿思想的全部。

sentences.en: And he's certainly in many covert ways advocated for organizations that supported civil and political rights for African Americans.
sentences.zh: 而且他肯定在许多暗地里的方式下，支持过那些为主张非裔美国人公民权利和政治权利的组织。

sentences.en: There's no question that he was maneuvering politically in public and behaving differently in private.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，他在公开场合进行政治手腕的操作，而在私底下则表现得截然不同。

sentences.en: The speech makes Washington a national figure.
sentences.zh: 这篇演讲让华盛顿成为了一个全国性人物。

sentences.en: Practically overnight, he becomes the most powerful Black man in the United States.
sentences.zh: 几乎在一夜之间，他成为了美国最具权势的黑人。

sentences.en: But it also opens a kind of schism.
sentences.zh: 但这也撕裂出了一道裂痕。

sentences.en: And Washington is about to meet an opponent who would challenge him over what freedom should look like.
sentences.zh: 而华盛顿即将迎来一位挑战者，对方将就自由应有的模样向他发起挑战。

sentences.en: Someone unwilling to compromise.
sentences.zh: 一个不愿妥协的人。

sentences.en: Someone ready to fight.
sentences.zh: 一个随时准备战斗的人。

sentences.en: Booker T.
sentences.zh: 布克·T·

sentences.en: Washington's ideas about Black education are about to meet their challenger,
sentences.zh: 华盛顿关于黑人教育的理念即将遭遇挑战者，

sentences.en: another intellectual heavyweight named W.E.B.
sentences.zh: 另一位重量级知识分子，名叫W·E·B·

sentences.en: Du Bois.
sentences.zh: 杜波依斯。

sentences.en: Du Bois also has a philosophy whose origins can be traced back to the blueback speller.
sentences.zh: 杜波依斯的思想渊源也可以追溯到那本蓝皮拼写书。

sentences.en: Only his experience with the book comes much later in life, because Du Bois is born into a much different world than Booker T.
sentences.zh: 只是他接触这本书的时间要晚得多，因为杜波依斯出生在一个与布克·T·大不相同的世界里。

sentences.en: Washington.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿。

sentences.en: Well, I want to bring in another historic figure, young W.E.B.
sentences.zh: 那么，我想引入另一位历史人物，年轻的W·E·B·

sentences.en: Du Bois.
sentences.zh: 杜波依斯。

sentences.en: He reads this speech after it gets published.
sentences.zh: 他在演讲发表后读到了它。

sentences.en: Where is Du Bois in his life at this point?
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，杜波依斯的人生处于什么阶段？

sentences.en: A little bit of his upbringing and how he sort of becomes an educator.
sentences.zh: 谈谈他的成长经历以及他是如何走上教育之路的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So part of what's really interesting about Du Bois is he and Washington are often positioned at odds, as they were.
sentences.zh: 关于杜波依斯，非常有趣的一点是，他和华盛顿经常被置于对立面，正如他们曾经那样。

sentences.en: But it's important to remember that, you know, Washington is sort of almost two decades older than Du Bois.
sentences.zh: 但重要的是要记住，华盛顿比杜波依斯大约了近二十岁。

sentences.en: It's actually only 12 years that separate Washington and Du Bois.
sentences.zh: 实际上，华盛顿和杜波依斯之间只相差十二岁。

sentences.en: But those dozen years between slavery and not slavery are a seismic shift.
sentences.zh: 但介于经历奴役与未经历奴役之间的这十二年，却是一次天翻地覆的巨变。

sentences.en: Washington, you know, is born in slavery.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿出生于奴隶制时期。

sentences.en: Du Bois is born in Great Barrington, Massachusetts, and has a very different kind of coming of age.
sentences.zh: 杜波依斯出生在马萨诸塞州的大巴灵顿，经历了截然不同的成长过程。

sentences.en: You know, doesn't have to walk 500 miles to get to school.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他不必走五百英里去上学。

sentences.en: And he is, you know, well-educated, a member of a very small black community in the Berkshires,
sentences.zh: 而且他受过良好的教育，是伯克希尔地区一个极小的黑人社区的一员，

sentences.en: where he's aware of being different and made aware in elementary school when he tries to give a valentine to a little girl who rejects it.
sentences.zh: 在那里他意识到了自己的与众不同，并在小学时尝试给一个小女孩送情人节卡片却遭到拒绝时，深深体会到了这一点。

sentences.en: And this becomes his moment of racial awareness, a racial reckoning.
sentences.zh: 这成为了他建立种族意识、经历种族觉醒的时刻。

sentences.en: But understood as extremely bright and talented.
sentences.zh: 但大家都知道他极其聪明且富有才华。

sentences.en: And when he graduates from high school, his mother dies when he's 17.
sentences.zh: 当他从高中毕业时，母亲在他17岁时去世了。

sentences.en: And so members of the local community put money together and sent him to Fisk University, which is the School of Classical Education for African-Americans at the time in Nashville.
sentences.zh: 因此，当地社区的成员凑钱把他送到了菲斯克大学，那是当时纳什维尔专门为非裔美国人设立的古典教育学校。

sentences.en: He wanted to go to Harvard undergraduate.
sentences.zh: 他原本想去哈佛读本科。

sentences.en: He winds up at Fisk.
sentences.zh: 最终他来到了菲斯克大学。

sentences.en: And Fisk is an extraordinary experience for him.
sentences.zh: 对而言，菲斯克是一段非凡的经历。

sentences.en: It's an outstanding institution.
sentences.zh: 这是一所杰出的学府。

sentences.en: And also for him, the first time he's around large numbers of African-Americans.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，这也是他第一次身处大量非裔美国人之中。

sentences.en: And these are really people who are amongst, you know, the best and brightest at that moment.
sentences.zh: 而且这些人确实是那个时期最优秀、最聪明的人才之一。

sentences.en: He's at Fisk, and in the summer after his sophomore year, as many students at historically black colleges at the time do, he finds a school to teach at during the summer.
sentences.zh: 他在菲斯克大学就读，在大二结束后的那个夏天，就像当时许多历史悠久的黑人大学的学生一样，他找了一所学校在夏天去教书。

sentences.en: This was a sort of routine process.
sentences.zh: 这算是一种例行程序。

sentences.en: And so if we say in Nashville in general, he learns about what Jim Crow looks like, right?
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们泛指纳什维尔的情况，他了解到了吉姆·克劳法是什么样的，对吧？

sentences.en: A comprehensive system of segregation, very different from the kind of racism that he experienced in Great Barrington.
sentences.zh: 一个全面的种族隔离体系，与他在大巴灵顿所经历的那种种族主义截然不同。

sentences.en: So at once, Fisk is this remarkable place that he falls in love with and also the place where he really understands what life is like for the majority of African-Americans.
sentences.zh: 因此，菲斯克大学瞬间成了他坠入爱河的奇妙之地，同时也是他真正理解大多数非裔美国人生活现状的地方。

sentences.en: So it's one level, but Nashville is a city, you know, in the summer, he goes out to rural Tennessee, very different kind of landscape.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是一个层面，但纳什维尔是一座城市，你知道的，到了夏天，他会去到田纳西州的农村，那是完全不同的风景。

sentences.en: People are really living at a subsistence level.
sentences.zh: 人们的生活确实只维持在勉强糊口的水平。

sentences.en: And it is here in this rural village that Du Bois will have a transformative experience with the Blueback Speller as a young teacher with a room full of black children in front of him.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个乡村里，年轻的杜波依斯作为一名教师，面对着一屋子的黑人儿童，通过《蓝皮拼写课本》经历了一次彻底改变人生的体验。

sentences.en: And he teaches at this school, and he talks about beautiful children with these bright and curious minds,
sentences.zh: 他在这个学校教书，讲到那些有着明亮而好奇的心灵的美丽孩子，

sentences.en: and he describes them sitting in front of the Blueback Speller and teaching them.
sentences.zh: 他描述他们坐在蓝背拼写课本前受教的情景。

sentences.en: Years later, Du Bois writes about those students, their bright but mischievous faces, bare feet swinging from rough benches, hands wrapped around the Speller.
sentences.zh: 多年后，杜波依斯写到了那些学生，他们明亮却顽皮的脸庞、从粗糙长凳上悬空摇晃的赤脚、双手紧紧握着拼写课本。

sentences.en: And he writes about encountering these students and how extraordinary they are and how they're learning in a context where the nation is supposed to be engaged in this progress,
sentences.zh: 他写到与这些学生相遇的经历，他们是多么非凡，以及他们在一个本该致力于进步的国家环境中学习，

sentences.en: but black people are being held back.
sentences.zh: 但黑人却受到了阻挠。

sentences.en: And then many years later, he returns to the school and finds that his prized pupil, Josie, has died.
sentences.zh: 又过了很多年，他回到学校，发现自己引以为傲的学生乔西已经去世了。

sentences.en: And so much of the promise has been snuffed out.
sentences.zh: 大部分的希望都被掐灭了。

sentences.en: Du Bois doesn't actually say how Josie dies, but in the intervening years, her family has fallen apart.
sentences.zh: 杜波依斯其实并没有说明乔西是如何去世的，但在那些年里，她的家庭已经四分五裂。

sentences.en: A brother in jail, a sister returning home with a child, and Josie carrying the weight of all of it, working, working, working herself to death.
sentences.zh: 一个兄弟入狱，一个妹妹带着孩子回到家中，而乔西独自扛下了这一切的重担，劳作、劳作、劳作，最终累死。

sentences.en: And that loss clarifies something for Du Bois.
sentences.zh: 而这种损失让杜波依斯看清了一些事情。

sentences.en: This story in some ways encapsulates why he becomes so resistant to his elder scholar, Booker T.
sentences.zh: 这个故事在某种程度上概括了他为什么会如此抗拒他的前辈学者布克·T·

sentences.en: Washington.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿。

sentences.en: Because what he shows is that even with all of the hard work, all of the possibility, all of the intellect and imagination,
sentences.zh: 因为他所展现的是，即便付出了所有的辛勤努力、拥有无限可能、具备所有的才智与想象力，

sentences.en: the brutality of the Jim Crow order is such that it destroys people's lives.
sentences.zh: 吉姆·克劳体制的残酷依然足以摧毁人们的生活。

sentences.en: And without access to suffrage, without access to full civil and political rights, no matter how hard you work, you're going to wind up with these devastating consequences.
sentences.zh: 如果没有选举权，没有完整的公民权和政治权利，无论你多么努力，最终都会落得如此毁灭性的结果。

sentences.en: To Du Bois, this idea that Washington has, that economic progress and hard work will lead to racial equality, just isn't real.
sentences.zh: 对杜波依斯而言，华盛顿那种认为经济进步和努力工作将带来种族平等的想法，根本是不切实际的。

sentences.en: And Josie is proof of that.
sentences.zh: 而乔西就是最好的证明。

sentences.en: He understands, to a certain extent, what Washington is trying to do, but he finds his acceptance of the constraints of Jim Crow unacceptable,
sentences.zh: 他在某种程度上理解华盛顿的意图，但他认为华盛顿对吉姆·克劳种种限制的顺从是无法接受的，

sentences.en: given the consequences of those constraints.
sentences.zh: 考虑到这些限制所带来的严重后果。

sentences.en: He channels all of this into a scathing critique of Booker T.
sentences.zh: 他将这一切倾注于对布克·T·

sentences.en: Washington in a chapter of The Souls of Black Folk, published in 1903.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿的猛烈批判中，这一批判收录于1903年出版的《黑人的灵魂》的一章里。

sentences.en: So he, you know, this is a really bold thing he does to write this book and to have this public criticism of, you know, this divide.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，他写这本书并对这种分歧进行公开批评，是一件非常大胆的事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, Du Bois, he has a chapter in The Souls of Black Folk called Mr. Booker T.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，杜波依斯在《黑人的灵魂》中有一章名为《布克·T·

sentences.en: Washington and others.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿及其他人》。

sentences.en: And he has a very direct and unflinching critique of Washington.
sentences.zh: 他对华盛顿进行了非常直接且毫不妥协的批判。

sentences.en: In some ways, his personal reflections are a bit gentler than what he publishes.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，他的个人反思比他公开发表的内容要温和一些。

sentences.en: But I think what he's trying to do is give voice to what a lot of Black intellectuals and activists and organizers are saying,
sentences.zh: 但我认为他试图做的是，为许多黑人知识分子、活动家和组织者一直在表达的心声发声，

sentences.en: which is what Washington is saying cannot be seen as speaking for Black people writ large, and certainly not the Black leadership class, as it were.
sentences.zh: 这也就是华盛顿的言论不能被视为代表广大黑人群体，当然更不能代表所谓黑人领导阶层的原因。

sentences.en: I think you can sum up Du Bois' critique like this.
sentences.zh: 我认为你可以这样总结杜波依斯的批判。

sentences.en: He believes that Booker T.
sentences.zh: 他认为布克·T·

sentences.en: Washington, by encouraging Black Americans to just focus on their own skills and financial independence and to wait for civil rights, to go slow,
sentences.zh: 华盛顿通过鼓励美国黑人只关注自身的技能和经济独立、等待民权、步调放缓，

sentences.en: that Washington is asking them to surrender something fundamental, their self-respect.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿是在要求他们放弃某些根本性的东西，即他们的自尊。

sentences.en: For Du Bois, the fight for civil rights and the vote cannot be pushed off into the future.
sentences.zh: 对杜波依斯而言，争取民权和投票权的斗争不能被推迟到未来。

sentences.en: How can someone defend his rights as a landowner or a business owner if he has no political power to do so?
sentences.zh: 如果一个人没有政治权力来捍卫自己的权利，他又该如何捍卫自己作为土地所有者或企业主的权益呢？

sentences.en: And he thinks Washington's focus on industrial education is part of the problem.
sentences.zh: 而且他认为华盛顿对实业教育的关注正是问题的一部分。

sentences.en: Instead of practical skills, Du Bois thinks that education for Black Americans should be broader,
sentences.zh: 杜波依斯认为，美国黑人的教育不应该局限于实用技能，而应当更加广泛，

sentences.en: a classical education, Greek, Latin, literature, philosophy,
sentences.zh: 即古典教育，涵盖希腊语、拉丁语、文学、哲学，

sentences.en: the kinds of subjects that could train a class of Black scholars, writers, and leaders.
sentences.zh: 那些能够培养出一批黑人学者、作家和领袖的学科。

sentences.en: He called this idea the talented 10th.
sentences.zh: 他将这个理念称为“天才十分之一”。

sentences.en: Du Bois gets a lot of criticism for his concept of the talented 10th that is also in that book,
sentences.zh: 杜波依斯因为其在这本书中提出的“天才十分之一”概念而受到了许多批评，

sentences.en: in which he says, essentially, you know, there's 10% of any community that are going to function as the leadership class,
sentences.zh: 他在书中基本上是说，你知道的，任何社群中都有10%的人将充当领导阶层，

sentences.en: and those people in the Black community should have access to, you know,
sentences.zh: 而黑人社群中的这些人应该有机会接触到，你知道的，

sentences.en: the highest level of education and classical education in particular.
sentences.zh: 最高水平的教育，特别是古典教育。

sentences.en: And on the one hand, while I think some of the critique is understandable,
sentences.zh: 一方面，虽然我认为其中一些批评是可以理解的，

sentences.en: I think given the context, it's important to keep in mind that if in general in the society,
sentences.zh: 但我认为结合当时的情境，有一点很重要，那就是如果在整个社会中，

sentences.en: people were saying, you know, Black people should only have access to industrial education,
sentences.zh: 人们普遍认为，你知道的，黑人只应该接受实业教育，

sentences.en: which really was the norm.
sentences.zh: 这在当时确实是常态。

sentences.en: He's saying in this, at least 10% of the Black population should have access to higher order education.
sentences.zh: 他在这其中表达的是，至少有10%的黑人人口应该有机会接受高等教育。

sentences.en: Because if not, then who is going to be in the rooms with white elites to advocate for Black people, right?
sentences.zh: 因为如果不这样，将来谁又能和白人精英共处一室来为黑人发声呢？

sentences.en: And so it sounds elitist, and in some ways it was, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此这听起来很精英主义，在某些方面也确实如此，你知道的，

sentences.en: and Du Bois, I think we can say in some ways wasn't elitist,
sentences.zh: 而杜波依斯，我认为我们也可以说他在某些方面并非精英主义，

sentences.en: but he's really trying to say we should not exclude Black people writ large from any sector of the society.
sentences.zh: 但他真正想表达的是，我们不应该把广大黑人排除在社会的任何领域之外。

sentences.en: And that was a bold statement.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很大胆的声明。

sentences.en: Du Bois also thinks there are consequences to Washington's accommodationist beliefs.
sentences.zh: 杜波依斯还认为，华盛顿的妥协立场会带来相应的后果。

sentences.en: He sees a direct line between the Atlanta Compromise speech and what came after.
sentences.zh: 他认为亚特兰大妥协演讲与随之而来的一切之间存在着直接的联系。

sentences.en: Just a year after Washington announced that the races could be as separate as fingers on a hand,
sentences.zh: 就在华盛顿宣布种族可以像手指一样分立的仅仅一年后，

sentences.en: the Supreme Court ruled in Plessy v.
sentences.zh: 最高法院对普莱西诉

sentences.en: Ferguson, making separate but equal the law of the land.
sentences.zh: 弗格森案做出了裁决，使“别而平等”成为全国的法律。

sentences.en: Du Bois thinks that Washington in the Atlanta Compromise speech gives up something that he had no right to give up, right?
sentences.zh: 杜波依斯认为，华盛顿在亚特兰大妥协演讲中放弃了他根本无权放弃的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: And sort of presented it as though Black Americans were willing to accommodate exclusion.
sentences.zh: 并且在某种程度上将其表现得好像美国黑人愿意顺从这种排挤一样。

sentences.en: And therefore that that sort of allowed for Plessy v.
sentences.zh: 因此，这在某种程度上使得普莱西诉

sentences.en: Ferguson to be decided without any anxiety on the part of the court.
sentences.zh: 弗格森案的裁决得以毫无法院的心理负担地做出。

sentences.en: Now, I think the reality is that regardless of what Washington had said,
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为现实情况是，无论华盛顿当时说了什么，

sentences.en: Plessy would likely have been decided the way that it was.
sentences.zh: 普莱西案的裁决结果很可能依然会是那样。

sentences.en: I think a better argument would be that Washington, you know, saw the way the wind was blowing
sentences.zh: 我认为一个更好的论点是，华盛顿，你知道的，看清了风向

sentences.en: and sort of said what he needed to say in order to continue to get financial support given the way the society was turning.
sentences.zh: 可以说为了顺应当时的社会风气，他说了他不得不说的话，

sentences.en: When Du Bois publishes The Souls of Black Folk in 1903, it lands hard.
sentences.zh: 1903年，当杜波依斯出版《黑人的灵魂》时，

sentences.en: The book is reprinted twice in its first two months.
sentences.zh: 这本书在头两个月内就再版了两次。

sentences.en: In some ways, it helps cement a certain kind of legacy for Booker T.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，它帮助布克·T·华盛顿

sentences.en: Washington,
sentences.zh: 巩固了某种历史遗产，

sentences.en: who is mostly remembered for his accommodationism.
sentences.zh: 人们对他的记忆大多停留在妥协立场上。

sentences.en: But Imani says he's actually much more complicated than that
sentences.zh: 但伊玛尼说，其实他远比这要复杂得多，

sentences.en: because of what he's doing behind the scenes with money he got from white donors,
sentences.zh: 因为他在幕后利用从白人捐赠者那里得到的资金做了很多事，

sentences.en: particularly when it comes to public education for Black children in the Jim Crow South.
sentences.zh: 特别是在吉姆·克劳时期的南方，涉及黑人儿童的公立教育时更是如此。

sentences.en: So Black students have fewer schools to attend.
sentences.zh: 因此，黑人学生可上的学校更少。

sentences.en: They often have shorter school terMs.
sentences.zh: 他们的学制通常也更短。

sentences.en: And they get much less money than schools for white students.
sentences.zh: 而且他们得到的资金远少于白人学校。

sentences.en: Many places, particularly rural places, don't have access to public schools at all.
sentences.zh: 许多地方，特别是农村地区，根本无法接触到公立学校。

sentences.en: And Southern states do not require schools that have been slated for white students
sentences.zh: 南方的州也不要求那些指定给白人学生的学校

sentences.en: to admit Black students even if they don't have an access to a local school.
sentences.zh: 接纳黑人学生，哪怕他们根本上不了当地的学校。

sentences.en: And it's sort of a long-winded way of getting to the point,
sentences.zh: 这可以说是绕了个大弯才说到点子上，

sentences.en: which is that Booker T.
